newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: ASEAN pledges to fight currency speculators.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN pledges to fight currency speculators.

text.p: Foreign ministers of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Friday pledged to jointly fight speculators selling down the region's currencies, the national Bernama news agency reported.

"Well-planned efforts to destabilise ASEAN currencies for self-serving purposes" threatens the stability of all its economies, they said in a joint communique at the close of the 30th ASEAN Ministerial Meeting, Bernama said.
The foreign ministers have called for intensification of cooperation between members to safeguard and promote ASEAN's interests in this regard, Bernama said paraphrasing from the statement.
Bernama said the communique, of which it had an advance copy, would be released later on Friday. It did not give any other details.
The ASEAN ministers statement followed a spirited verbal attack from Malaysia's Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad against "rogue speculators" out to "undermine" economies of the region.
He also hinted at a possible common law in the ASEAN region to fight currency speculation.
ASEAN, or the Association of South East Asian Nations, groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam and, since Wednesday, Laos and Burma.
